newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay index rebounds, hopes of political solution.
newsitem.headline: Bombay index rebounds, hopes of political solution.

text.p: Bombay shares rebounded in afternoon trade on Friday from an early slump on expectations of a solution to the political crisis, brokers said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index was up 2.56 points at 3,600.93 after sliding to 3,512.05.
India's ruling United front and ally-turned-foe, the Congress party, were holding talks on Friday to find a successor to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, leaders of both sides said in New Delhi.
They said a consensus candidate for the top job could be named by the United Front before a parliamentary vote of confidence scheduled for later on Friday, or soon afterwards.
"This is good news. It looks like the crisis has been averted," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities.
At 0825 GMT the Bombay share index was up 26.62 points, or 0.74 percent, at 3,624.99.
